newsitem.title: POLAND: Centertel to operate Polish DCS mobile system.
newsitem.headline: Centertel to operate Polish DCS mobile system.

text.p: The Polish Telecommunications Ministry has chosen analogue mobile phone operator PTK Centertel to operate a digital DCS mobile network, newspapers reported on Saturday.
Only Centertel from seven prospective bidders had submitted a final application for a licence to operate the network.
"We're glad the ministry so highly appraised our offer and we'll try not to disappoint our clients," Centertel deputy director general Krystyn Antczak told daily Rzeczpospolita.

Antczak would not say how much Centertel would pay for the concession but the daily Gazeta Wyborcza, citing unofficial sources, said Centertel would pay $80 million up front and a further $20 million in five annual instalments.
Wyborcza said the new system would start up around the end of this year and that the whole network would be in place by the end of next year.

Last month Poland's tender committee said the licence for the the DCS system, issued together with a permit to cover the territory of at least 10 Polish provinces, would be granted by the Telecommunications Ministry by mid-September.
Centertel, in which state-owned telecoms monopoly TPSA and France Telecom have 66-percent and 34-percent stakes respectively, launched operations in Poland in 1991.
The DCS system is a more advanced version of the popular Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM) cellular telephone system, using a higher frequency of 1800 MHz instead of GSM's 900 MHz.
Centertel remains a market leader with over 185,000 customers but GSM competitors Era GSM and GSM Plus are expanding rapidly.
